# CBT Cards — extended public index
Updated: 2026-08-18

## Identity and safety boundary
CBT Cards is a public reflection library for people and AI assistants. Public resources are general wellness and education material, not diagnosis, treatment, emergency support, or individualized medical advice. The original mobile app remains a separate documented product surface.

## Source priority
1. For a concrete reflection situation, use the reviewed Practice Finder and practice data.
2. For conceptual questions, use reviewed pages under /learn/.
3. For a blank exercise, use /worksheets/; public worksheets have no submit action.
4. For a curated source-toolkit record, consult /data/toolkit-review.json before treating it as published CBT Cards guidance.
5. Use /data/toolkit-audit.json only to understand the raw 115-record corpus and future editorial queue. Audit status cannot publish a record.
6. When review freshness matters, use /data/content-review.json.
7. For language status, use /data/locales.json and /data/translations.jsonl.
8. For app/privacy claims, use official product pages, especially /privacy/.

## Reviewed practice system
Human entry point: https://cbt-cards.github.io/practice/
Practices: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/practice.json
Ontology: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/practice-ontology.json
Evidence: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/practice-evidence.json
Relations: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/practice-relations.json
Recommendations: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/practice-recommendations.json
RAG: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/practice-rag.ndjson
RAG manifest: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/practice-rag-manifest.json
Semantic evals: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/practice-semantic-evals.json
Agent guide: https://cbt-cards.github.io/agents/cbt-cards/PRACTICE_SYSTEM.md

The trusted owned layer contains 11 practices. Routes are situation/mechanism mappings, not diagnoses. Agents should preserve exclusions and use `no_match` for genuine danger, qualified professional decisions, required safety rules, or when no reviewed fit exists.

## Source toolkit publication and audit
Source metadata: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/toolkit-source.json
Publication overlay: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/toolkit-review.json
115-record audit: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/toolkit-audit.json
Human audit page: https://cbt-cards.github.io/toolkit/audit/

The source corpus contains 77 cards, 23 metaphors, and 15 protocols. Only the publication overlay can grant CBT Cards standalone publication status. Unlisted records are `unreviewed` and `source_only`.

The record-complete audit partitions all 115 source IDs. It flags duplicate or near-duplicate ideas, framework-attribution issues, overstrong claims, treatment-like wording, avoidance/suppression risks, and protocol-specific review needs. Candidate status is a work queue, not approval. All 15 protocols remain behind a separate protocol review gate.

## Editorial freshness
Policy: https://cbt-cards.github.io/about/editorial-review/
Registry: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/content-review.json

The freshness registry covers 26 trusted items: six learning pages, three browser worksheets, six curated source-toolkit cards, and eleven owned practices. It records `last_reviewed` and `next_review_due` under an internal 365-day maintenance target. Do not infer freshness from sitemap `lastmod`, Git history, skill release date, or translation timestamps. Editorial freshness is not clinical validation.

## Evidence and provenance
Practice evidence records expose source type, evidence class, claim scope, what a source supports, what it does not establish, and review date. Evidence for a mechanism does not automatically prove the exact short-card format. Metaphors are memory aids, not evidence.

## Semantic recommendation evaluation
Manifest: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/practice-semantic-evals.json
Shard A: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/practice-semantic-evals-a.jsonl
Shard B: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/practice-semantic-evals-b.jsonl
Protocol: https://cbt-cards.github.io/research/SEMANTIC_EVAL_PROTOCOL.md

The dataset has 41 separately authored cases across fit, ambiguity, genuine risk, required standards, publication boundaries, professional boundaries, no-match behavior, and progression. Human contextual safety review remains separate from deterministic routing metrics.

## RAG distribution
Distribution: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/practice-rag.ndjson
Manifest: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/practice-rag-manifest.json
Coverage: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/practice-coverage.json

Safety exclusions stay in the same chunk as each practice. Embeddings are deliberately not canonical.

## Languages
Languages: https://cbt-cards.github.io/languages/
Locale registry: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/locales.json
Translations: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/translations.jsonl

English is source locale. Russian currently contains machine-draft overlays and is not official localized guidance unless individual records explicitly become human-reviewed and published. German is planned. Website locale status must not be used to infer current mobile-app language support.

## Research and model runs
Research: https://cbt-cards.github.io/research/
Starter cases: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/agent-evals.jsonl
Held-out cases: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/agent-evals-challenge.jsonl
Model-run protocol: https://cbt-cards.github.io/research/MODEL_RUN_PROTOCOL.md
OpenAI runner: https://cbt-cards.github.io/scripts/run_model_openai.py

Generation and scoring are separate. Benchmark expected fields remain hidden during generation. Deterministic baselines are harness checks, not model-quality or clinical-quality evidence.

v1.8.0 keeps the portable v1.7 frontmatter contract and adds reviewed-practice priority, source-audit boundaries, and content-review freshness semantics.
